summary:
I've spent the past couple of weeks replacing Hermes-Agent with a personal assistant built on the Claude Agent SDK. The trigger was a small skill, turning on a light when a meeting starts, that the local Qwen model couldn't do. It made 65 tool calls and never ran the command. The new version talks to me over Telegram and sends anything private to a narrow local-model lane. The boundaries are enforced with separate unix users, not by asking the model to behave. Adding five tool servers cost 83.5K tokens per session, and one network server was about 65K of that. I deferred that server, which brought the cost back to about 21K.

Then I gave it a web app, installable on a phone. Most of the work was iPhone quirks. Safari won't play Ogg Opus, so the app serves MP3. Audio created after a reply arrives gets blocked, so one audio element is unlocked on a tap and reused. In standalone mode on iOS 18, the layout height came up 62 pixels short and iOS painted the gap. I added a launch log that reports the real viewport numbers, so I stopped guessing at the fix. Sonnet agents wrote most of the UI overnight, each in its own worktree. I orchestrated, merged and deployed, and the suite sat at 964 tests by the end.

On the tabletop side, I built a public Foundry module that imports sessions from a D&D companion app. The worst bug was a reveal poller that stalled and looked like a hung call. The real cause was that Foundry cleans creation data in place, deleting undefined fields from the objects you pass in, including the key the plan used later. The fix was to capture keys before the create and pass copies. After that the module passed 27 of 27 checks against a real Foundry install, and the secret-leak gates all stayed green.

Among the Internal MCP Servers, the useful find was why the assistant kept "ignoring instructions" and writing its own scripts. FastMCP defaults to stateful sessions, so any restart gave the next call "Session not found". The model was handed a broken tool and improvised around it. I set stateless mode on the three servers and restarted each a few times to confirm the sessions survived.

highlights.oneLiner: Replaced it with a Claude Agent SDK assistant after Qwen made 65 calls, ran nothing.
Stateless mode fixed 'Session not found'; model stopped improvising around dead tools.
Routes private requests to a narrow local-model lane, kept apart by unix users.
Rebuilding the platform on Fastify, TypeScript and Postgres.
